segments.text: I asked my coding agent for one small thing: give the top bar a bit more room. It changed two lines of CSS. Looks fine, right? So the agent runs Selfie review. That renders every story in our storybook, 124 of them, in a pinned container right here on this MacBook Air. 25 seconds with no cloud and no bill per image. What comes back is one JSON document and an exit code, so any agent can read it. Exit one, because that two-line change touched all 124 stories. Now it's my turn. The Selfie UI command opens the same review for a person. 124 changed and nothing decided yet. That's a lot to look at, but Selfie works out what kind of change each one is. 48 of them only moved or gained spacing with nothing new in the image. Here's one. Yellow is spacing that grew. Press F and the two images flip in place so you can see exactly what moved. That looks right, so I approve those 48 together. But what about dark mode? I search for dark, and there it is, 85,000 changed pixels. The agent hardcoded a light color, and the top bar went white. I don't have to describe where. I click the change, write what's wrong, and send it to the agent, which has been waiting. The agent gets my words, the story, the exact box, and a picture of what I saw. It puts the theme's color back, renders again, and answers my note. Selfie tells me there's a newer batch, and the reply is right there on the story. The bar is dark again, and 85,000 changed pixels are down to 13. I resolve the note and approve the rest. The 48 I already approved are simply unchanged now, because an approval follows your Git history. The agent commits and reviews once more. It's the exact same build, so nothing renders. A third of a second and exit zero. Push it, and Selfie renders in CI and puts a status on the commit. Click through, and it's the same review in the cloud. Selfie works with any coding agent. If you have a storybook, start locally today at selfie.dev and join the waitlist for the cloud.
